<info added on 2025-07-10T19:11:00.943Z>

Implemented thread-safe transitions using semaphores with timeout handling and emergency recovery mechanisms. Added stack usage monitoring via uxTaskGetStackHighWaterMark. tasks.title: Implement Alarm Notification Sound Functionality
tasks.description: Add audio playback capabilities for timer completion alerts, including SD card sound storage, web-based configuration for sound selection and preview, and ESP32-S3 I2S audio output implementation.
tasks.details:
Research and implement I2S audio playback on ESP32-S3-Touch-AMOLED-1.75 using the built-in speaker. The device has an AXP2101 power management IC that controls speaker power via GPIO. Implementation steps:

1. **Hardware Configuration**:
   - Identify I2S pins for the built-in speaker (typically I2S_BCK, I2S_WS, I2S_DOUT)
   - Configure AXP2101 to enable speaker power when needed
   - Research ESP32-S3 I2S driver configuration for mono speaker output

2. **SD Card Audio Storage**:
   - Create /sounds directory on SD card for alarm audio files
   - Support WAV format (16-bit, 44.1kHz recommended for ESP32)
   - Implement SD card file listing for available sounds
   - Add default alarm sound to firmware (fallback if SD unavailable)

3. **Audio Playback System**:
   - Use ESP32 I2S library for audio output
   - Implement WAV file parser for header reading
   - Create non-blocking audio playback using DMA buffers
   - Add volume control (0-100%) stored in NVS
   - Implement fade-in for gentle alarm start

4. **Web Configuration Interface**:
   - Add /api/sounds endpoint to list available alarm sounds
   - Create /api/sounds/preview/:filename for sound testing
   - Add settings page section for alarm configuration:
     - Enable/disable alarm toggle
     - Sound selection dropdown
     - Volume slider (0-100%)
     - Preview button for each sound
   - Store alarm preferences in NVS

5. **Integration with Timer System**:
   - Modify TimerState to trigger alarm on completion
   - Add alarm cancellation on any user interaction
   - Implement alarm timeout (30 seconds max)
   - Visual indication during alarm (LED flash pattern)

6. **Power Management**:
   - Enable speaker power only during playback
   - Ensure proper cleanup on sleep transitions
   - Handle alarm during low battery gracefully

Code structure:
```cpp
class AlarmController {
  void begin();
  void playAlarm(const char* filename);
  void stopAlarm();
  void setVolume(uint8_t vol);
  bool isPlaying();
  std::vector<String> listSounds();
};
```
tasks.testStrategy:

tasks.title: Implement External Button for Deep Sleep/Wake Control
tasks.description: Add support for a physical external button on GPIO19 that acts as a simple on/off switch, triggering deep sleep when pressed while awake and waking the device when pressed during deep sleep.
tasks.details:
Implementation requires careful handling of ESP32-S3 deep sleep wake sources and GPIO configuration:

1. **GPIO Configuration**:
   - Define EXTERNAL_SLEEP_BUTTON_PIN as GPIO_NUM_19 in firmware.ino
   - Configure GPIO19 with internal pull-up resistor using gpio_set_pull_mode()
   - Set up falling edge interrupt for button press detection when awake
   - Ensure GPIO19 is available as RTC GPIO (verified for ESP32-S3)

2. **Button Interrupt Handler**:
   ```cpp
   void IRAM_ATTR onExternalButtonPress() {
     static unsigned long lastPress = 0;
     unsigned long now = millis();
     if (now - lastPress > 200) { // Debounce 200ms
       externalButtonPressed = true;
       lastPress = now;
     }
   }
   ```

3. **Sleep State Modifications**:
   - Add new sleep trigger type: SLEEP_TRIGGER_EXTERNAL_BUTTON
   - Modify enterDeepSleep() in SleepState.cpp to accept trigger parameter
   - Store sleep trigger in RTC memory to distinguish wake source
   - Configure wake source based on trigger:
     ```cpp
     if (trigger == SLEEP_TRIGGER_EXTERNAL_BUTTON) {
       // Only external button can wake
       esp_sleep_enable_ext0_wakeup(GPIO_NUM_19, 0); // Wake on LOW
     } else {
       // Existing inactivity sleep - keep touch/encoder wake
       configureInactivityWakeSources();
     }
     ```

4. **Wake Detection**:
   - Check esp_sleep_get_wakeup_cause() on boot
   - If ESP_SLEEP_WAKEUP_EXT0, device was woken by external button
   - Clear any sleep trigger flags stored in RTC memory

5. **State Machine Integration**:
   - Add external button check in main loop
   - When externalButtonPressed flag is set:
     - Save current state to RTC memory if needed
     - Call enterDeepSleep(SLEEP_TRIGGER_EXTERNAL_BUTTON)
   - Button should work from any state (Idle, Timer, Paused, etc.)

6. **Hardware Wiring**:
   - Connect momentary pushbutton between GPIO19 and GND
   - No external pull-up resistor needed (use internal)
   - Button press pulls GPIO19 LOW, release returns HIGH
   - Consider adding 100nF capacitor for hardware debouncing

7. **Power Considerations**:
   - Deep sleep triggered by external button uses minimal power
   - Only RTC domain remains powered for wake detection
   - Ensure AXP2101 power management allows RTC GPIO wake

8. **Conflict Avoidance**:
   - Keep existing BOOT button (GPIO0) functionality separate
   - Don't modify existing inactivity sleep behavior
   - External button provides dedicated hardware on/off control
tasks.testStrategy:
1. **Basic Button Functionality**:
   - Wire button to GPIO19 and GND
   - Verify internal pull-up keeps pin HIGH when not pressed
   - Test button press detection with Serial.println() in interrupt handler
   - Confirm debouncing prevents multiple triggers

2. **Sleep Trigger Testing**:
   - Press external button while device is awake
   - Verify device enters deep sleep immediately
   - Check current consumption drops to ~10μA range
   - Confirm display, LEDs, and all peripherals power down

3. **Wake Testing**:
   - With device in external-button-triggered deep sleep
   - Press external button and verify device wakes
   - Confirm touch screen does NOT wake device
   - Confirm encoder rotation does NOT wake device
   - Verify only external button can wake from this sleep mode

4. **State Preservation**:
   - Start timer, then press external button
   - Wake device and verify timer state is lost (expected)
   - Document that external button sleep doesn't preserve state

5. **Inactivity Sleep Isolation**:
   - Let device sleep via 3-minute inactivity timeout
   - Verify touch and encoder still wake from inactivity sleep
   - Confirm external button also wakes from inactivity sleep
   - Test that both sleep modes work independently

6. **Edge Cases**:
   - Rapid button presses (test debouncing)
   - Button held down (should trigger once)
   - Button press during state transitions
   - Power-on with button already pressed

7. **Integration Testing**:
   - Test external button from each state (Idle, Timer, Paused, etc.)
   - Verify no interference with existing UI interactions
   - Confirm WiFi/web server state after wake
   - Test with production test suite to ensure compatibility

tasks.title: Implement thetimer.app OAuth Integration
tasks.description: Replace manual webhook/API key configuration with automated OAuth flow allowing users to click 'Connect to thetimer.app', authenticate via popup, and automatically receive API credentials.
tasks.details:
Implementation requires comprehensive OAuth 2.0 flow integration:

1. **OAuth Client Configuration**:
   - Register device application with thetimer.app OAuth provider
   - Configure redirect URIs for device web interface
   - Store client ID and secret securely in device firmware
   - Implement PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) for enhanced security

2. **Web Interface Updates**:
   - Add 'Connect to thetimer.app' button to device settings page
   - Implement OAuth popup window using window.open() with proper dimensions
   - Handle postMessage communication between popup and parent window
   - Display connection status with visual indicators (connected/disconnected)
   - Show connected account information and disconnect option

3. **OAuth Flow Implementation**:
   - Generate authorization URL with state parameter and PKCE challenge
   - Handle authorization callback with code exchange for access token
   - Implement token refresh mechanism for long-term connectivity
   - Store tokens securely in device NVS with encryption

4. **API Integration**:
   - Replace manual webhook configuration with OAuth-authenticated API calls
   - Implement automatic project sync from thetimer.app account
   - Add real-time timer status updates to connected thetimer.app account
   - Handle API errors gracefully with user-friendly messages

5. **Security Considerations**:
   - Implement proper CSRF protection using state parameter
   - Validate all OAuth responses and handle edge cases
   - Secure token storage with device-specific encryption keys
   - Add token expiration handling and automatic refresh
tasks.testStrategy:
1. **OAuth Flow Testing**: Test complete authorization flow from button click to token receipt, verify popup window opens correctly and handles user authentication, confirm postMessage communication works between popup and parent window

2. **Connection Status Validation**: Test connection status display updates correctly after successful OAuth, verify disconnect functionality removes stored tokens, confirm reconnection works after disconnect

3. **API Integration Testing**: Test automatic project sync from connected thetimer.app account, verify timer status updates are sent to thetimer.app during timer sessions, confirm error handling when thetimer.app API is unreachable

4. **Security Validation**: Test CSRF protection by manipulating state parameters, verify tokens are stored securely and encrypted in NVS, confirm token refresh works before expiration, test behavior with expired or invalid tokens

5. **Edge Case Testing**: Test behavior when popup is blocked by browser, verify handling of network connectivity issues during OAuth flow, test multiple rapid connection attempts, confirm graceful degradation when OAuth fails
